items.title: Maryland sues UnitedHealth for $380M over ‘defective computer system’ - HealthExec
items.reason: This is a state attorney-general enforcement action against a major payer (UnitedHealth) alleging system defects, directly matching the topic's focus on payer litigation and regulatory sanctions.
items.summary: Maryland's Attorney General filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth seeking $380 million in damages, alleging that the company operated a defective computer system that resulted in improper claims processing and payments. The suit represents a significant state-level enforcement action against one of the nation's largest health insurers. Revenue-cycle teams are affected because claims processing defects at major payers can directly impact denial rates, payment accuracy, and appeal workflows for provider organizations.
